title: BOB user plugin file (~/.config/bob/services.d/*.json) — schema v1
description:
Accepted shapes for a user plugin file under schema v1:

  1. RAW ARRAY (legacy / current default) — a bare JSON array of Service objects, identical to services-list.schema.json. This is what every plugin file is today.

  2. WRAPPED OBJECT (forward-compat) — a JSON object with a `schema_version` integer and a `services` array. The wrapper exists so future schema migrations can be gated cleanly: each major schema bump (v2, v3…) ships its OWN plugin-file.schema.json at a NEW $id. The current file is the v1 validator and accepts only schema_version=1 by design — a v2 plugin file must be validated against the v2 schema, not this one.

  Reserved-for-future field names within the wrapper (`metadata`, `disabled`, `overrides`) are intentionally rejected today via additionalProperties:false, so no current plugin author defines them in a way that would collide with the meaning v2/v3 will assign. They will become active properties (with their own validation) in the schema version that introduces them.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE — runtime fallback. The runtime loader (bob.registry._extract_plugin_entries) treats a bare array as semantically equivalent to {schema_version: 1, services: [...]}. This fallback is a runtime convenience for legacy plugins; it is NOT enforced by this JSON Schema (a raw array stays a raw array as far as JSON Schema is concerned).

This meta-schema does NOT validate cross-service uniqueness or other runtime invariants — see service.schema.json scope notes.

schema_version.description: Major version of the BOB plugin contract this file targets. This v1 validator accepts only schema_version=1 — that is intentional: a v2 plugin must be validated against the v2 plugin-file.schema.json (which will live at a different $id), not this one. Without that strict gating, this validator could silently 'accept' a v2 plugin without applying any v2 rules.
